text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's industrial output declined in October and will keep falling in the next three months, the Warsaw School of Economics Economic Development Institute said.
- In the first nine months of this year, 321,000 passenger cars and 33,000 commercial vehicles were sold, the Samar monitoring agency said. Polish-made passenger cars accounted for 69% of the sales.
- Thomson Consumer Electronics Poland plans to sell 150,000 television sets in 1996 and increase its market share by four percent which will earn it net revenues of 150 million zlotys.

- The Polska Zegluga Baltycka (PZB) shipping company introduced a discount return ticket offer worth 100 Swedish crowns valid in November on the Malmo-Swinoujscie route which is addressed to Sweden-based customers. The offer should offset the company 's losses over the "dead season".

- The Polish LOT national air carrier's sister company Eurolot will take over LOT's European regional connections as of spring 1997. The new regional carrier will fly Canadian-made Jet Stream aircraft which can take up to 20 passengers.
- In many respects Poland was the most successful country in implementing free-market reforms, a recently-published report by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said.
- Polish-Russian trade liberalisation will profit Poland, Poland's Foreign Trade Minister Janusz Kaczurba said. However, the free trade zone talks should not be hurried, he said.
- One in three companies in the former communist central European countries is Polish, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's food prices in the first 10 days of November went up by 1.8 percent compared with the last 10 days of October and by two percent compared with the same period last month, GUS said.
- Polish air carrier LOT's privatisation advisor will be chosen in the first half of 1997 through a tender, Poland's Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said.

- Polish-Hungarian trade turnover grew by 30 percent in the first eight months of 1996 with Polish exports to Hungary growing faster than the other way, the Budapest-based Polish Embassy Commercial Counsellor Edward Molendowski said.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Polish government economic committee KERM has approved the introduction of licenses for car assembly in Poland.
- The Volkswagen Group plans to buy buildings for assembly of cars in Jelenia Gora province, west Poland, VW Group said.
- The Wroclaw branch of the Plus GSM digital mobile phone company has gained 870 subscribers in the first two weeks of operation, the company said.
- Daewoo Motor Poland has been licensed to assemble 20,000 Nexia cars in the Lublin-based plant in the next three years, Centrum Daewoo deputy director Sang Heun Lee said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The listed Budimex construction firm will build a bio-treatment section of the Gdansk sewage treatment plant worth 188 million zlotys.

- The Polish language version of the European Planete documentary channel will be available to viewers daily from 7 a.m. to 2 a.m. on cable TV as of December 2 this year, a Planete network representatives said.
- Poland's state treasury has sold to France's Otor company a 51 percent stake in the SilesianPap paper mill in southern Poland, the state treasury said.
ZYCIE
- The French Lafarge cement company has acquired a control stake in the Wierzbica cement mill despite the protests by the plant's trade unions. Lafarge now holds a 60 percent stake in the mill.
- In the first ten months of 1996 the Poznan-based Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) bank exceeded by 30 percent its results for the same period last year.
- Poland's average monthly salary in the public sector in October was 6.2 percent higher than in September, GUS said.
PARKIET

- October was a very good month for most companies listed on the Warsaw bourse and they reported their biggest profits so far this year. The companies' strong results stemmed mostly from operational activity.
- The Bank Handlowy Capital Operations Centre (BH COK) recommends buying shares of Gdynia-based Bank Komunalny to medium-term investors in a report dated October 10.
